text:
lina_support: Escalation from Acme: customer hit by duplicate charge and intermittent 401s after upgrading to ts-sdk@2.4.1. Billing team flagged two identical POSTs.
acme_support: Their logs show two POST /v1/charges 800ms apart, different X-Request-ID headers but identical JSON body. No Idempotency-Key present. Running on GCP Cloud Run; Node v20.5, undici 5.16, plus a shared lib that vendored undici 5.10.
jin_eng: please paste request IDs and a minimal repro if they have one. Also confirm whether the app reuses AbortController across retries.
acme_support: req IDs: req_A1B2C3D4, req_A1B2C3D5. They sent a short repro snippet — simple retry wrapper that reuses the same AbortController for retry attempts.
acme_support: ```js
const ctrl = new AbortController();
try {
  await client.post('/v1/charges', { body: JSON.stringify(payload), signal: ctrl.signal });
} catch (err) {
  await sleep(150);
  // reuse same ctrl.signal for retry
  await client.post('/v1/charges', { body: JSON.stringify(payload), signal: ctrl.signal });
}
```
mel_sdk: reusing the same signal on retry is an anti-pattern. With undici + Node, that can result in either an already-aborted signal being observed or body stream reuse leading to duplicate server-side processing. Additionally, if the SDK performs an auth refresh and replays the request without an Idempotency-Key, duplicates happen.
opsbot: attached log snippet from customer:
[2026-03-15T20:12:07.123Z] POST /v1/charges req=req_A1B2C3D4 200 210ms
[2026-03-15T20:12:07.320Z] auth: token refresh triggered (401) -> refresh start
[2026-03-15T20:12:07.450Z] POST /v1/charges req=req_A1B2C3D5 200 190ms
mel_sdk: note both requests returned 200-level responses but billing shows two captures. Likely flow: first request processed, auth middleware returned transient 401 during refresh, client retried and caused duplicate capture.
adrian_sre: are they rotating credentials mid-flight? Any short-lived tokens? That could explain auth-refresh races.
acme_support: they use short-lived tokens and an in-app refresh that races with requests. Token refresh logs show a 401 from our auth endpoint followed by successful refresh.
jin_eng: reproduction plan:
1) local Node v20.5 + undici 5.16 + ts-sdk@2.4.1
2) simulate auth endpoint returning 401 for refresh while main API processes request
3) run with (a) reusing AbortController across retries and (b) creating fresh controller per attempt
4) run with single undici vs. mismatched vendored undici to see signal semantics
mel_sdk: immediate mitigations for customer:
- Add an Idempotency-Key header to billing POSTs (recommended) — stops duplicate captures immediately.
- Stop reusing AbortController across retry attempts; create a fresh controller per try.
- Test isolation of undici versions (ensure only one copy on runtime). We saw undici 5.10 + 5.16 in the stack.
- Try ts-sdk@2.4.3-canary: we patched signal replay in canary.
jin_eng: I reproduced the duplicate POST locally when reusing the same AbortController: SDK sends the first request, then on auth-refresh replay it sends another with same body. No error thrown. Patch strategy: ensure we do not reuse an AbortSignal across attempts; create an internal controller per attempt and proxy cancellation.
mel_sdk: product-side actions:
- Short-term: advise customers to always include Idempotency-Key for non-idempotent endpoints.
- Medium-term: add a safeguard in SDK: when retrying POSTs due to auth-refresh and no Idempotency-Key present, log a warning and refuse to auto-replay the body unless caller opts into replay.
- Add a docs section explicitly stating AbortController reuse is unsupported for retries.
lina_support: told customer to add idempotency key and to test the canary. Customer reported that adding Idempotency-Key prevented duplicates in their next test run.
opsbot: ticket updated: priority=high, assigned=mel_sdk, followup=24h
mel_sdk: I'll open PR to implement the warning + opt-in replay flag and cut ts-sdk@2.4.3-canary. If urgent, we can backport a hotfix to 2.4.x.
acme_support: escalation requested to high; billing team requires root cause and timeline for fix.
jin_eng: additional note: bundling/multiplexing undici versions (app + shared lib) can change AbortSignal behavior. Recommend customers avoid vendoring undici or ensure runtime single copy.
adrian_sre: long-term: consider SDK-level auto-idempotency for known billing endpoints or a required Idempotency-Key validation when doing retries after auth refresh.
lina_support: thanks all. I'll update Acme once canary build is available and include the reproduction steps and recommended mitigations. :pray:
